channel.title: Retirement on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Retirement on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: macOS 14 runner image retirement
item.description:
GitHub Actions will retire the macOS 14 runner image on November 2, 2026. Before removal, jobs that use macOS 14 will temporarily fail during scheduled awareness periods.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Virtual Machines will be retired on October 31, 2029
item.description:
DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Linux, Windows, and Dedicated Host virtual machines will be retired on October 31, 2029. After that date, they will no longer be available for use or purchase, so workloads should be migrated before then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: NVv3-series Azure Virtual Machines
item.description:
Microsoft Azure retired several NVv3-series virtual machine sizes on September 30, 2026. Any remaining NVv3-series VMs are also being retired.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VMs
item.description:
Microsoft announced retirement of the Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VM series in public cloud regions. These VM families will reach end-of-life on November 15, 2029.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps
item.description:
Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps will be retired on September 29, 2027. After that date, existing v1 apps will stop running and will no longer handle requests or event-driven triggers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Arc enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager will be retired September 30, 2029
item.description:
Microsoft will retire Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) on September 30, 2029. Customers using it should plan to transition to an alternative solution before that date.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Microsoft HPC Pack
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring all versions of HPC Pack. It is entering a one-year retirement period with limited retirement-only support, and end of support is August 27, 2027.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
item.description:
Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029. Microsoft says you can keep using it until then, but recommends starting transition planning early as Azure IoT evolves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Communication Services (ACS) standalone services will be retired on September 30, 2028
item.description:
Microsoft will retire several standalone Azure Communication Services offerings on September 30, 2028. After that date, the affected services will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026. Azure Function apps using 7.4 will keep running, but security updates and customer support stop, so users should move to PowerShell 7.6.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 ends on November 10, 2026—upgrade your apps to .NET 10
item.description:
Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 in Azure Functions ends on November 10, 2026. Apps will keep running, but they will no longer receive security updates or support for those runtimes, so migrate to .NET 10 before the deadline.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node.js 22 ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node.js 22 in Azure Functions ends on April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security patches, updates, and support for Node.js 22 will stop; move to Node.js 24 by then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement Update: SAP container images removed October 14, 2026
item.description:
SAP container images are scheduled for removal on October 14, 2026. The containerized SAP data connector retired on September 14, 2026 and is now unsupported and unmaintained, though existing TLS-compliant agents can still send logs through the retired HTTP Data Collector API.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service
item.description:
Support for Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service ends on December 10, 2026. After that date, new Azure Linux with OS Guard clusters cannot be created, and Azure Container Linux is the replacement.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: aks: AppNet 2026-08-19
item.description:
AppNet 2026-08-19 adds public preview availability in more Azure regions, retires AppNet 1.0–1.2, and updates supported versions to Istio 1.28.10, 1.29.6, and new AppNet 1.5 on Istio 1.30.3. The release also includes fixes for cluster validation, gateway CRD conflicts, certificate rotation, multicluster traffic, identity-based updates, cleanup on delete/leave, diagnostics, and clearer error reporting.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node 22 LTS ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node 22 LTS on Azure App Service ends April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running after that date, but security updates and customer support for Node 22 LTS will stop.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution License-included service will be retired August 30, 2027
item.description:
Azure VMware Solution license-included service will be retired on August 30, 2027. The change follows Broadcom’s updated VMware licensing policy requiring customers on hyperscaler platforms to bring their own portable VMware Cloud Foundation license.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications
item.description:
Microsoft will retire the containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications on September 14, 2026. After that date, the agent will be permanently disabled and will stop sending SAP logs to Microsoft Sentinel.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Nested confidential (cc_v5) VMs will be retired on September 1, 2026
item.description:
Azure will retire the cc_v5 confidential VM series on September 1, 2026. After that date, the affected VM sizes will no longer be available for use or purchase, and any impacted VM not resized beforehand will be deallocated.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Retiring the Copilot Billing Preview app
item.description:
GitHub has retired the Copilot Billing Preview app and it is no longer available. Copilot spend can now be reviewed and managed directly in GitHub billing settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Models is now retired
item.description:
GitHub Models was retired on July 30, 2026. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) access are no longer available to customers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release 2026-07-17
item.description:
AKS v20260717 adds Artifact Streaming GA, new preview networking and scheduling features, and multiple behavior changes and bug fixes. It also updates Kubernetes patch versions, core add-ons, node images, and includes several retirement notices and upcoming defaults.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Python-2.7; 3.8 and PowerShell- 7.1; 7.2 will be retired on September 30, 2026
item.description:
Azure Automation will stop supporting Python 2.7, Python 3.8, and PowerShell 7.1/7.2 starting October 1, 2026. Runbooks may still run, but these runtimes will no longer receive security updates or bug fixes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot Billing Preview app will be retired on August 3
item.description:
GitHub will retire the Copilot Billing Preview app on August 3, 2026. Users who rely on it for Copilot spend review are directed to use built-in GitHub visibility instead.

  • Source: GitHub
